hero.title: Stream Sniping Detector
hero.lead: A desktop tool that reads your PUBG match history and surfaces the patterns behind suspected stream sniping — recurring opponents, match overlap rates and proximity timelines.
hero.meta: Windows and macOS · Installer, portable or universal app

overview.title: Read the match history, not the stream
overview.lead: Stream sniping is when a player watches someone’s live broadcast to gain an unfair tactical advantage. Doing it leaves a trace in the match history: running into the same opponent far more often than chance would explain. This tool makes that trace measurable.
overview.noteText: The application never follows matches in progress — it only reads data from completed matches through the official PUBG API.

installation.title: Up and running in three steps
installation.lead: Windows and macOS. The macOS build is not notarised by Apple, so it ships with an installer that clears the quarantine flag for you.

download.title: Download the latest release
download.body: Grab the most recent build from the GitHub Releases page.

run.title: Run the application
run.body: On Windows, run the installer or double-click the portable build — no installation needed. On macOS, unzip the download and double-click Install.command (right-click → Open if macOS blocks it); it copies the app to Applications and opens it.

analyse.title: Start analysing
analyse.body: Enter a player name to pull their recent match history and inspect the overlaps.

installation.securityTitle: Download from the official links only
installation.securityText: Builds are published on GitHub Releases, and the updater checks each one against its SHA-256 checksum before installing. A copy from anywhere else skips that check, so treat it as untrusted.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: What the tool is, what it is not, and where its data comes from.

cheat.q: Is this a cheat or a hack?
cheat.a: No. It is not a cheat, a hack or any kind of game modification. It never touches the game: no files, no memory, no injection, no overlay. It is a separate desktop application that reads publicly available match records after the fact, the same way a stats website does.

background.q: Does it run in the background while I play?
background.a: No. It only runs while you have it open, and it never follows a match in progress. There is no background service, no process watching the game and nothing real time about it. It reads the history of matches that have already ended.

data.q: Where does the data come from?
data.a: Entirely from the official PUBG API. Every number you see (shared matches, overlap rates, proximity timelines) is derived from the match data that API returns. Nothing is scraped from the game client and nothing is guessed.

ban.q: Can using it get my account banned?
ban.a: The application does not interact with the game or its client in any way; it only queries an official, public API. That said, only the game's own operator can make statements about accounts. This project is not affiliated with PUBG or KRAFTON.

verify.q: How do I know the download is genuine?
verify.a: Official builds exist in one place: the GitHub Releases page linked from this site, which is where the download button points. Updates are verified against their published SHA-256 checksum before they are installed, so a file altered on the way does not pass. That check only covers builds from the official links, so treat a copy from anywhere else as untrusted.

proof.q: Does a high overlap rate prove someone is stream sniping?
proof.a: No. It is a signal, not a verdict. A high rate of shared matches and close encounters means the pattern is unlikely to be chance, but region, playtime and queue times all shape the numbers. The tool measures the pattern; the conclusion is yours.
